---
title: "Where Sessions Started"
description: "Sessions that included a Signal Check or dashboard, by where the session started."
---

Where readers came from when they opened a Signal Check or a dashboard: Slack,
Teams, email, one of our own links, no link recorded, or another site.

**The source belongs to the session, not the page.** Google Analytics records
where a session started, then credits every page in it. So "Slack, 20 sessions"
on a page means 20 sessions that started from a Slack link and opened this page
at some point. It does not mean 20 people clicked a Slack link to this page: a
reader who came from Slack to a Signal Check and then followed a link to a
dashboard counts as a Slack session on the dashboard too.

## Calculation

From [`meta_page_traffic`](../../catalog/google_analytics/meta_page_traffic.qmd),
sum `sessions` by page and source group over the reporting window. The groups map
`sessionsource`:

| Group | `sessionsource` |
|---|---|
| Slack | `slack` |
| Teams | `teams`, or anything starting `teams.` |
| Email | `email` |
| Our own links | `latest-link`, `report_link`, `dashboard_link` |
| No link recorded | `(direct)`, `(not set)` |
| Other sites | anything else |

The Readership dashboard's `source_group()` holds the same map; change both
together.

*Our own links* are the link to the latest Signal Check and the links inside a
Signal Check or a dashboard. *No link recorded* is a bookmark, a typed address,
or an app that drops the link's source.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Example queries"}

::: {.panel-tabset}

## SQL

```sql
SELECT
    pagepath_redacted,
    CASE
        WHEN sessionsource = 'slack' THEN 'Slack'
        WHEN sessionsource = 'teams' OR starts_with(sessionsource, 'teams.') THEN 'Teams'
        WHEN sessionsource = 'email' THEN 'Email'
        WHEN sessionsource IN ('latest-link', 'report_link', 'dashboard_link') THEN 'Our own links'
        WHEN sessionsource IN ('(direct)', '(not set)') THEN 'No link recorded'
        ELSE 'Other sites'
    END AS source_group,
    SUM(sessions) AS sessions
FROM google_analytics.meta_page_traffic
WHERE page_kind IN ('signal_check', 'dashboard')
  -- set the reporting window; see the timespans note in cookbook/notes.qmd
  AND CAST(date AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2026-09-01' AND DATE '2026-09-30'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY pagepath_redacted, sessions DESC, source_group;
```

## R

```r
tbl(con, in_schema("google_analytics", "meta_page_traffic")) |>
  filter(
    page_kind %in% c("signal_check", "dashboard"),
    # set the reporting window; see the timespans note in cookbook/notes.qmd
    as.Date(date) >= as.Date("2026-09-01"),
    as.Date(date) <= as.Date("2026-09-30")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    source_group = case_when(
      sessionsource == "slack" ~ "Slack",
      sessionsource == "teams" | substr(sessionsource, 1, 6) == "teams." ~ "Teams",
      sessionsource == "email" ~ "Email",
      sessionsource %in% c("latest-link", "report_link", "dashboard_link") ~ "Our own links",
      sessionsource %in% c("(direct)", "(not set)") ~ "No link recorded",
      TRUE ~ "Other sites"
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(pagepath_redacted, source_group) |>
  summarise(sessions = sum(sessions, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(pagepath_redacted, desc(sessions), source_group)
```

:::

:::

## Interpretation notes

**Sessions add up within a page, not across pages.** One session that opened two
pages counts once on each, so the sessions on two pages together can exceed the
sessions that reached either of them. For a whole product, sum per page and say
"sessions that included a page", or count each session once in the GA4 interface.

**For a Signal Check, use its first 14 days.** That is when the announcement posts
send their readers. See [Signal Check Views](signal-check-views.qmd) for the
window.

## Alternative names

- traffic sources
- referral sources
- where readers came from
- session source
